input.original_text: The (3+1)-dimensional KdV-ZK problem has produced several families of accurate traveling-wave solutions when the uniﬁed approach method is applied. These solutions are stated in terms of rational, trigonometric and hyperbolic functions. These solutions are categorized into three distinct sets based on the parameters obtained from the balancing procedure and auxiliary Riccati equation. • Set I corresponds to the case where F1 = 0, leading to solutions that include bright/dark soliton proﬁles for N < 0 and periodic wave patterns for N > 0. • Set II and Set III incorporate non-zero F1 and exhibit combined soliton structures, including singular periodic waves and complex-valued wave proﬁles. • Graphical simulations conﬁrm the physical realism of these solutions, showcasing wave propagation, amplitude variation, and localization features in 2D, 3D and density plots. The bifurcation analysis of the equivalent planar Hamiltonian system reveals that the nature of solutions is governed by the signs of parameters A and B: • For R > 0,S > 0, The system supports both periodic and homoclinic orbits (solitary waves) and admits three equilibrium points: a saddle at the origin and two centers. • For R > 0,S < 0, only a saddle point exists, precluding periodic solutions. • For R < 0,S < 0, two saddle points connected by heteroclinic orbits indicate kink/antikink solutions whereas periodic orbits round the origin, which turns into a center. These phase portraits provide a complete qualitative description of all possible wave patterns supported by the model, linking analytical solutions directly to dynamical systems theory. In this work, a mixed analytical and dynamical approach is used to explore the (3+1)-dimensional KdV-ZK problem. The available solution set of the model is greatly increased by using the uniﬁed technique, which is demonstrated to be an eﬀective tool for generating a wide class of accurate soliton solutions, including kink-type, singular and periodic waves. The simpliﬁed dynamical system’s basic phase-space structure is revealed by complementary bifurcation analysis, which makes it possible to categorize wave behaviors according to equilibrium stability and parameter variations. This combined method oﬀers a dynamical explanation for the development of wave solutions in addition to precise formulations for them. The results have applications in ﬂuid dynamics, nonlinear optics and plasma physics, where localized wave phenomena are crucial. In addition to applying the concept to additional higher-dimensional nonlinear evolution equations, further research may concentrate on symmetry reductions, conservation laws and stability characteristics of the found solutions.

canonical.abstract: In Part I [J. Math. Phys. 40, 1595 (1999)] we studied eigenfunctions of the quantum dynamics that defines the two-particle relativistic Calogero–Moser system with elliptic interaction. In the present paper we consider the same system with hyperbolic and trigonometric interactions. In these special regimes the eigenfunctions are shown to admit an elementary representation that is far more explicit than the “zero representation” of Part I. In particular, the new representation can be exploited to prove that the hyperbolic eigenfunctions can be chosen to be symmetric under interchanging position and momentum variables (self-duality). In the trigonometric case duality properties are derived, too, and several orthogonality and completeness results are obtained.
